how: The surface view of Neptune made by functions (deep.ts). Lengths are in units of the close scene: the planet's radius is close.json radius, the camera of the approved close image stands 1 unit over the deck. u runs along the band (the great circle through closeup.json band), v across it, both from the point under that camera's nadir line; heights are over the smooth deck. Times are seconds from the middle of the surface view. Nothing here is a picture: every value below feeds a function of place, height and time. on: true draws this scene in the surface view and, by the eye's height, on the globe in the dive and the rise (globe below), so the film never shows two different places.

globe.how: The same scene on the globe in the dive and the rise; nothing here reads the clock. height: the eye's height over the planet in radii at which the scene first shows and at which it is drawn whole; between them it comes in over the globe's own map by the logarithm of the height. border: degrees from the place on the ground between which the scene ends and the globe's own map goes on (the horizon is 14 degrees away at 0.03 radii, so the surface view's field lies inside). fall: one grade for the globe and the scene by the eye's height, the way from the azure planet of the hold to the navy deck of the approved close image. Measured on globe alone against scene alone at 4715 to 4730 (assets-src/neptune/NOTES.md, 24 Nov 00:12): the pale band has one colour on both (pivot, linear light), the dark of the scene is the globe's to a power. Under the pivot a channel is drawn as pivot times (colour over pivot) to an exponent, over it unchanged: on the globe the exponent goes from 1 at the first height to power at the second, on the scene from 1 over power to 1, by the logarithm of the height. At the hold (2.07 radii) the globe is untouched, under the second height the scene is. On the globe and in the far look of the scene the grade is one text (planet.ts, FALL_GLSL), and there a colour off the pivot's own line keeps its hue: its level is its green over the pivot's green, its red is the smaller of the channel's own value and the colour times what the grade does at that level, its blue the larger. So a colour bluer than the pivot (the deck) is drawn channel by channel as before, and a dim white under the pivot stays white: drawn channel by channel it kept its red and lost its green and blue, which were the orange specks of the dim side at 4988 and 4707 and the lilac on the bands at 4720 (assets-src/neptune/NOTES.md, 24 Nov 16:05 to 17:10). blue: the most blue a graded colour of the globe keeps, as a multiple of its green, at the second height (over it the limit is this over the share of the grade, so there is none at the first height): the powers draw a deep blue of the map out to cobalt (seen at 4716 to 4720), the scene's own deck stands at 2.7. grid: a tool, 1 draws the scene's own coordinates on the deck, 2 and 3 write u and v of the deck under each pixel into the layers view (two bytes over 48 units, for measures); 0 in the film.

far.how: The far look of the scene: the globe's own map (its deck, its cloud layer and that layer's shadow), read in the scene's shader by the very lines the globe draws with (planet.ts, mapGlsl) and from the globe's own uniforms, so that what is far in the scene is the picture the globe showed from above. distance: the distance on the ground from the place (the point under the eye of the judged surface frame), in units of the scene, from which the map begins to show and at which it is the whole picture; nearer than the first the scene's own deck and cirrus stand alone, so no point of the ground changes its picture because the eye moves. One field by place alone (MAIL 774): the law that weighed the map against the scene by the eye's height is deleted, with its numbers. The map gives the tone and the pattern at every wave it holds, at every height; the scene's deck multiplies it by one number for all three colours, its own light over the light of the same deck made of nothing but waves of length wave and longer (flat lit, without the storm, the cirrus or its shadow), at most the factor most. Where a pixel covers such a wave the two are one and the map stands untouched. Above globe.height the scene as a whole is not drawn yet and the place's own share is drawn alone over the globe. Nothing here reads the clock. on: 1 the film, 0 none of it, 2 the map alone at every distance (a tool). The colour is the globe's own: the map's deck and cloud under the globe's own curves of light, then the globe's own grade of the fall (globe.fall; planet.ts, FALL_GLSL, the one text of it) at the strength the globe has at this height, with what the end of the scene's shader does to every channel undone beforehand, so that the far look stands where the globe's picture stands at every height. tone, power, cloud: trims on the deck (a power, then a factor) and on the cloud layer (a factor) before that grade; 1 is none.

fan.how: The veil: a thin sheet of ice haze over the deck, laid by place on the ground and ended by place (from, to across the flow along a tilted line; west along it). The view fan of the surface camera that once cut it is deleted (MAIL 774, MAIL 806 point 4): nothing here is weighed by a picture's foot. height: its lower and upper end; depth: its optical depth straight down; layers: taps through it; fall: the power by which it thins upward; light: what it scatters, in the colours of the hold (it is laid on before the grade of the fall, deep.ts underAir); shade: its share between the deck and the Sun; tilt, from, to, west: where it lies; wave, long, contrast, share, sizes: its bands along the flow.

steps.how: deck: steps of the relief march; shade: steps toward the Sun over the deck's own relief; cirrus: the most steps through the cirrus, each cirrusShare of its distance from the eye long; cirrusLimit: the shortest wavelength the cirrus keeps, in steps; light: taps toward the Sun inside the cirrus, the first lightStep long and each lightGrow times the one before, reading no wavelength shorter than lightLimit of the tap; cast: taps through the cirrus shell from the deck toward the Sun. cirrusSkip: where a step of the march finds the bent place outside every body, the march, the taps toward the Sun and the taps of the shadow go on by this share of its distance from the nearest body before they read again (0: every step is read). cirrusOpaque: the march ends where less than this share of what lies behind still comes through the cirrus. lightDeep: the optical depth toward the Sun past which the taps stop, since no light of the Sun comes through that the picture could show.

storm.how: at: u, v of the middle. eye: radius of the bowl. wall: shares of the eye radius between which the wall falls. depth: of the floor under the deck. reach: radius inside which the streaks wind round the storm. arms: count, pitch (turn per e-fold of radius; of the deck's octaves round the storm the longest take it whole and those as long as broad take none, deck lump), height, core (added to the radius under the logarithm), warp, light (how far an arm lifts the brightness), from (the shares of the eye radius between which the arms set in: under 1 they wind into the eye, so the eye is a whirl with a floor and no dark disc with a rim drawn round it). ragged: how far the deck's structure moves the wall in and out. spin: degrees a second at the middle, radius of half speed, share of it the arm pattern turns at. rings: the share of the deck's contrast the winding streaks keep at the storm's middle (they are fine rings, not a whirl). dark: the share of its brightness the deck loses on the floor of the eye. collar: the paler ring round the eye that the approved close image has: the radius from and to over which it ends, how far it lifts the brightness, and the share of it that follows the thin streaks, so the rim is made of streaks that fade outward and not of a disc with an edge. arms.light 0.2 and the third of collar 0.12 since 25 Nov (0.6 and 0.3 before): on a deck level of 0.75 the arms and the collar stood on the top of the albedo, a pale disc with a ring that showed from the hold (MAIL 840 points 2 and 5).

wind.how: deck: speed along the band, jet (its swing across the band), jetWidth (units per radian of the swing), phase. cirrus: speed along the band and its shear across (per unit). row: the size of the rows (and rings) an octave rides in, in its own wavelengths.

deck.how: wave: the longest wavelength of the deck's structure. stretch: how far the longest octave is drawn out along the wind (share of its length across). lump: the power of the wavelength by which a shorter octave is drawn out less, until it is as long as broad (0: all octaves alike, streaks at every size), so the long waves are bands and the short ones cloud; the octaves round the storm follow the same rule from spiral.along up to spiral.across. curl: how far an octave is carried across the wind by each longer one, in wavelengths of that longer one (0: straight streaks). gain: weight of each octave against the one before. relief: height of the rolls. march: the shortest wavelength the relief march follows (finer relief shades by its slope only). life: how fast an octave of wavelength 1 changes of itself (per second, grows as the wavelength falls). colours are linear light before the film's exposure and tone curve: night (lowest), blue (middle), pale (highest). contrast: how far the structure moves the brightness. near: v from, v to over which the thin streaks set in (wisp.near is the share they keep south of it), a zone by place on the ground. bounds: the highest and the lowest the deck can stand, for the march. level: the brightness without structure (0.75: at 0.55 the detail stood across the knee of the three tones at 0.5 and every lump flipped between night and pale, the speckle of the plain). The zones that drew the tones of the approved close image on the ground (the lift of the pale deck outside the dark oval, the drop of the near deck, the drop west of the storm inside the view fan) are deleted with their numbers (MAIL 774): the long waves of tone are the map's.

wisp.how: The thin bright streaks: the ridges of the octaves from number from on, each raised to power, each weighing gain of the one before; light: how far they lift the brightness; mean: what is taken off so the deck keeps its level; where: the range of the structure over which they come in. limit (above): the shortest wavelength drawn, in footprints of a pixel on the deck. near: the share of the streaks the dark near deck keeps. far: v from, v to over which the streaks of the far field grow, and how much more they lift the brightness there (the approved close image has long fine streaks along the limb).

cirrus.how: shell: lowest and highest height any cirrus can stand at. streamers (the first three are those of the approved close image; the fourth is the bright bow west of the storm and the fifth the band of cirrus on the far rim of the dark oval, both where the globe's own map has them from above): line (u from, u to, v at from, v at to), bow (how far its middle stands across the straight line, so it runs as an arc), wide (the width at the two ends as shares of halfWidth), halfWidth, base (height of its underside), thick, density, ends (length over which it fades at each end), lump (length of its thick and thin parts), lumpShare, seed, bend (the share of the bend of the line, warp below, that this streamer takes: 1 whole, less for a thin far one that stays a line), where (all: everywhere; map: a streamer of the globe's own map that the approved close image does not have, it ends at the border of the fan). lee: how much wider the side away from the Sun trails; leeSun: the same for the side toward the Sun (1: as wide as the crest). wave, stretch, rise, gain, octaves: the noise that tears it (rise: how far it is drawn out upward against across). erode: how much of the body the noise eats; soft: the density range over which it sets in. sigma: extinction per unit of density and length. A streamer is a chain of heaps with fibres blown off it (assets-src/neptune/NOTES.md, 24 Nov 02:57 to 03:11). The heaps: the narrow crest of the body, eaten by the noise, the density by the square so the edges are soft; core: the share of that eating the middle of the crest is spared. The fibres: the whole body with its trail on both sides, of density leeThin against the heaps, eaten 1 plus leeErode times as much; fringe: the density range over which the fibres set in, the share of the trail the side toward the Sun has, and the heights (shares of the thickness) between which the fibres end upward. billow: how far the first octaves are drawn out along the wind (near 1: round heaps) and how many they are; the finer ones are drawn out to stretch where the trail is. sweepDeg: the angle the grain of the noise stands at to the wind. warp, warpWave, warpNext: how far and at what wavelength the line of a streamer is bent, and size and reach of each next bend against the one before. floor: what is taken off the body so that it ends. castWave: the shortest wavelength of the noise that the shadow on the deck reads; cast: how many times its own depth toward the Sun the cirrus takes from the deck's light (the fibres finer than castWave are not in the shadow's taps). life: how fast an octave changes of itself. thin: a streamer narrower than the foot it is read with is not drawn at that distance: what is drawn of its density is whole while two pixels are under the first share of its width and none from the second on (0.1 and 0.33: whole from a width of 20 pixels, none under 6), and its thick and thin parts (lump) go to their mean by the same law against their length, so a far streamer thins away and never breaks up into a row of dashes (MAIL 840 point 1).

haze.how: Two layers of air whose density falls with height: low (the bright line at the limb and the pale far deck) and high (the wide blue glow). depth: optical depth straight down from space; scale: the height over which it falls by e; colour: what it scatters of white sunlight. forward: weight and sharpness of the lobe toward the Sun. top: height where the drawn shell ends. share: the strength of the air's own light, as a part of the Sun's. The air is light added along the path, after the end's grade of the fall: L = G(L0) * T + G(S) * (1 - T), T one number for the three channels, G the grade of the fall's end (none at the ground, so there L = L0 * T + S * (1 - T)). S is lit by the globe's own curve of light at the place (curve.json deck, its green over the curve's top), so air and deck have one Sun, and behind the cirrus it takes the shadow the deck under it has. low 0.065 and 0.028, share 0.45 since 25 Nov, 06 h (0.05, 0.045 and 0.25 before, under a law that graded the air with the deck and let thin air through as (1 - T) to the fall's powers, 4.5 times more in red than in blue: the orange and violet band at the far limb and a plain that stayed navy).

light.how: sun: the strength of the far Sun (linear light before exposure). sky: what the deck gets from above without the Sun. cloud: what the cirrus gets from the deck below and from the air. forward: weight and sharpness of the cirrus's lobe toward the Sun. wrap: how far the deck's light wraps past the edge of the Sun's reach. through: what the cirrus lets down to the deck beside the straight beam, light scattered on through the cloud: its share and how fast it dies with the cloud's depth, so the shadow of a streamer is dark and not black. cirrus: the share of the Sun the cirrus sends on. deep: light that reaches the inside of a cloud by scattering, twice a share and how fast it dies with the depth toward the Sun. shadow: how soft the shade of the deck's own relief is. shade: how dark the deck's own shadow is at its darkest, as the share of the Sun it takes (1 took all of it and the grade of the fall drew the rest as navy chunks, MAIL 840 point 1; 0.25). shadeFoot: the height over which that shadow sets in for each unit of the foot a pixel has on the ground, so its edge is never cut sharper than the pixel that shows it; the relief that casts is read no finer than that foot (deep.ts).
